subject: Maths
title: Cartesian Product & Relations
formula:
n(A × B) = n(A) · n(B)
Total subsets of A = 2ⁿ, Total relations from A to B = 2^(n(A)·n(B))
n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B)
n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(A∩B) - n(B∩C) - n(A∩C) + n(A∩B∩C)
notes: A relation R is reflexive if (a,a) ∈ R, symmetric if (a,b)∈R ⇒ (b,a)∈R, transitive if (a,b),(b,c)∈R ⇒ (a,c)∈R. An equivalence relation satisfies all three.

subject: Maths
title: Compound & Multiple Angles
formula:
sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B
cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B
tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B) / (1 ∓ tan A tan B)
sin 2A = 2sin A cos A = (2tan A)/(1 + tan²A)
cos 2A = cos²A - sin²A = 2cos²A - 1 = 1 - 2sin²A = (1 - tan²A)/(1 + tan²A)
tan 2A = (2tan A)/(1 - tan²A)

subject: Maths
title: Transformation & Triple Angle Formulas
formula:
sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2)
sin C - sin D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) sin((C-D)/2)
cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2)
cos C - cos D = -2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((C-D)/2)
sin 3A = 3sin A - 4sin³A
cos 3A = 4cos³A - 3cos A
tan 3A = (3tan A - tan³A) / (1 - 3tan²A)
notes: Essential for converting product of trigonometric functions into sums/differences for integration and algebraic simplification.

subject: Maths
title: Modulus, Argument & Polar Form
formula:
z = x + iy   ⇒   |z| = √(x² + y²)
Conjugate: z̄ = x - iy,   z · z̄ = |z|²
Polar Form: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = r e^(iθ)
Euler: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ,   i² = -1, i³ = -i, i⁴ = 1
notes: Argument θ = tan⁻¹|y/x| placed in correct quadrant. For ax² + bx + c = 0 with D < 0, roots are x = (-b ± i√(4ac - b²)) / (2a).

subject: Maths
title: Roots & Nature of Discriminant
formula:
x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a)
Sum of roots: α + β = -b/a,   Product of roots: αβ = c/a
Equation: x² - (Sum)x + (Product) = 0
notes: D = b² - 4ac. If D > 0: Real & Distinct; D = 0: Real & Equal (x = -b/2a); D < 0: Complex conjugate pair. If a,b,c are rational and D not a perfect square: conjugate surds.

subject: Maths
title: Arrangements & Selections
formula:
ⁿPᵣ = n! / (n - r)!
ⁿCᵣ = n! / (r! · (n - r)!)
ⁿCᵣ = ⁿC_{n-r}
Pascal Identity: ⁿCᵣ + ⁿC_{r-1} = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ
Total selections from n items: ⁿC₀ + ⁿC₁ + ... + ⁿCₙ = 2ⁿ
notes: Arrangement of n items where p are of one kind, q of another: n! / (p! · q!). Circular permutations of n distinct items: (n - 1)!.

subject: Maths
title: General & Middle Term
formula:
(a + b)ⁿ = Σ_{r=0}^{n} ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ
General Term: T_{r+1} = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ
Middle Term: If n is even, term is T_{(n/2)+1}. If n is odd, terms are T_{(n+1)/2} and T_{(n+3)/2}.
notes: Number of terms in (a + b)ⁿ is n + 1. Sum of coefficients in (1 + x)ⁿ is 2ⁿ. Ratio of consecutive terms: T_{r+1} / Tᵣ = ((n - r + 1) / r) · (b / a).

subject: Maths
title: AP, GP & Special Sums
notes: Arithmetic Mean A = (a + b)/2, Geometric Mean G = √(ab). For positive real numbers: A ≥ G.

subject: Maths
title: Forms of Equation & Angle
formula:
Slope-Intercept: y = mx + c
Point-Slope: y - y₁ = m(x - x₁)
Two-Point: (y - y₁) / (y₂ - y₁) = (x - x₁) / (x₂ - x₁)
Intercept Form: x/a + y/b = 1
Perpendicular Distance from (x₀,y₀) to Ax + By + C = 0: d = |Ax₀ + By₀ + C| / √(A² + B²)
Angle between two lines: tan θ = |(m₂ - m₁) / (1 + m₁m₂)|
notes: Lines are parallel if m₁ = m₂. Lines are perpendicular if m₁ · m₂ = -1. Distance between parallel lines: d = |C₁ - C₂| / √(A² + B²).

subject: Maths
title: Circle, Parabola, Ellipse & Hyperbola
formula:
Circle: (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r²
Parabola (y² = 4ax): Focus (a,0), Directrix x = -a, Latus Rectum = 4a
Ellipse (x²/a² + y²/b² = 1, a > b): b² = a²(1 - e²), Foci (±ae, 0), Latus Rectum = 2b²/a
Hyperbola (x²/a² - y²/b² = 1): b² = a²(e² - 1), Foci (±ae, 0), Latus Rectum = 2b²/a
notes: Eccentricity e = c/a: Circle e = 0, Parabola e = 1, Ellipse e < 1, Hyperbola e > 1. Rectangular hyperbola has e = √2.

subject: Maths
title: Standard Limits & First Principle
formula:
lim_{x→0} (sin x / x) = 1,   lim_{x→0} (tan x / x) = 1
lim_{x→0} (eˣ - 1) / x = 1,   lim_{x→0} (ln(1 + x) / x) = 1
lim_{x→a} (xⁿ - aⁿ) / (x - a) = n · aⁿ⁻¹
First Principle: f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x + h) - f(x)] / h
Product: (uv)' = u'v + uv',   Quotient: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv') / v²
notes: Standard derivatives: d/dx[xⁿ] = nxⁿ⁻¹, d/dx[sin x] = cos x, d/dx[cos x] = -sin x, d/dx[tan x] = sec²x, d/dx[sec x] = sec x tan x, d/dx[eˣ] = eˣ, d/dx[ln x] = 1/x.

subject: Maths
title: Variance, Standard Deviation & Axioms
formula:
Mean: x̄ = (Σxᵢ) / n = (Σfᵢxᵢ) / N
Variance: σ² = (Σ(xᵢ - x̄)²) / n = (Σxᵢ² / n) - (x̄)²
Standard Deviation: σ = √(Variance)
Coefficient of Variation: C.V. = (σ / x̄) · 100%
Probability: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
notes: For mutually exclusive events: P(A ∩ B) = 0 ⇒ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B). A series with lower C.V. is more consistent/stable.

subject: Physics
title: Dimensions, Errors & Vernier
formula:
Principle of Homogeneity: Dimensions on LHS = Dimensions on RHS
Absolute Error: Δaᵢ = |a_mean - aᵢ|
Relative Error = Δa_mean / a_mean,   Percentage Error = (Δa_mean / a_mean) · 100%
Propagation: Z = A · B ⇒ ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B;  Z = Aⁿ ⇒ ΔZ/Z = n · (ΔA/A)
Least Count: Vernier = 1 MSD - 1 VSD; Screw Gauge = Pitch / Total circular scale divisions
notes: Dimensions of Planck constant h: [ML²T⁻¹], Gravitational constant G: [M⁻¹L³T⁻²], Viscosity η: [ML⁻¹T⁻¹], Surface tension T: [MT⁻²].

subject: Physics
title: 1D Motion & Projectile Motion
formula:
v = u + at,   s = ut + ½at²,   v² = u² + 2as
s_nth = u + ½a(2n - 1)
Projectile Motion:
Time of Flight: T = (2u sin θ) / g
Maximum Height: H = (u² sin²θ) / (2g)
Horizontal Range: R = (u² sin 2θ) / g
Trajectory Equation: y = x tan θ - (g x²) / (2u² cos²θ)
notes: Maximum range occurs at θ = 45°: R_max = u²/g. Range is equal for complementary angles θ and (90° - θ).

subject: Physics
title: Force, Friction & Banking
formula:
Newton's 2nd Law: F⃗ = dp⃗ / dt = m a⃗
Impulse: J⃗ = F⃗_avg · Δt = Δp⃗
Static Friction: f_s ≤ μ_s N,   Kinetic Friction: f_k = μ_k N
Angle of Repose / Friction: tan θ = μ_s
Safe speed on banked road: v = √[ r·g · (tan θ + μ) / (1 - μ tan θ) ]
Optimal speed (no wear & tear): v_opt = √(r · g · tan θ)
notes: Newton's 3rd Law: Action and reaction forces act on two different bodies and never cancel each other. Apparent weight in accelerating lift: W = m(g ± a).

subject: Physics
title: Work-Energy Theorem & Collisions
formula:
Work: W = F⃗ · s⃗ = F s cos θ
Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = ΔK = ½mv² - ½mu²
Potential Energy of Spring: U = ½kx²
Power: P = dW / dt = F⃗ · v⃗
1D Elastic Collision:
v₁ = [(m₁ - m₂) / (m₁ + m₂)]u₁ + [2m₂ / (m₁ + m₂)]u₂
v₂ = [2m₁ / (m₁ + m₂)]u₁ + [(m₂ - m₁) / (m₁ + m₂)]u₂
notes: Coefficient of restitution e = (v₂ - v₁) / (u₁ - u₂). e = 1 for perfectly elastic, e = 0 for perfectly inelastic collision (bodies stick together).

subject: Physics
title: Torque, Angular Momentum & MOI
formula:
Center of Mass: r⃗_cm = (Σmᵢ r⃗ᵢ) / Σmᵢ
Torque: τ⃗ = r⃗ × F⃗ = I α⃗
Angular Momentum: L⃗ = r⃗ × p⃗ = I ω⃗
Conservation of Angular Momentum: If τ_ext = 0 ⇒ I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂
Rotational K.E.: K_rot = ½ I ω²,   Total Rolling K.E.: K = ½mv²(1 + k²/R²)
Parallel Axis: I = I_cm + Md²;   Perpendicular Axis: I_z = I_x + I_y
notes:
Moments of Inertia:
Ring (axis perp to plane): MR²
Disc (axis perp to plane): ½MR²
Solid Cylinder: ½MR²
Solid Sphere: ⅖MR²
Hollow Sphere: ⅔MR²
Rod (axis through center): (1/12)ML²

subject: Physics
title: Kepler's Laws & Escape Velocity
formula:
Gravitational Force: F = G · (m₁ m₂) / r²
Acceleration due to gravity: g = GM / R²
Variation with height h (h << R): g_h = g(1 - 2h/R)
Variation with depth d: g_d = g(1 - d/R)
Gravitational Potential: V = -GM / r,   P.E. U = -GMm / r
Orbital Velocity: v_o = √(GM/R) = √(gR) ≈ 7.92 km/s
Escape Velocity: v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR) = √2 · v_o ≈ 11.2 km/s
notes: Kepler's 3rd Law: T² ∝ r³. Geostationary satellite: Time period = 24 hours, height ≈ 36,000 km above Earth's surface, rotates from West to East.

subject: Physics
title: Hooke's Law, Bernoulli & Viscosity
formula:
Stress = F / A,   Strain = ΔL / L
Hooke's Law: Stress = Y · Strain   (Y = Young's Modulus)
Bulk Modulus: B = -ΔP / (ΔV/V),   Compressibility = 1/B
Pascal's Law: Pressure P = F/A is transmitted equally in all directions
Equation of Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂
Bernoulli's Theorem: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = Constant
Stokes' Law: F_v = 6πηrv,   Terminal Velocity: v_t = 2r²(ρ - σ)g / (9η)
Surface Tension: T = F / L,   Excess Pressure: Drop ΔP = 2T/R; Soap Bubble ΔP = 4T/R
Capillary Rise: h = (2T cos θ) / (r ρ g)
notes: Torricelli's Law of efflux: v = √(2gh). Venturimeter uses Bernoulli's principle to measure liquid flow rate.

subject: Physics
title: Heat Transfer & First Law
formula:
Linear Expansion: ΔL = L₀ α ΔT,   Area: β = 2α,   Volume: γ = 3α
Heat: Q = mcΔT,   Latent Heat: Q = mL
Rate of Heat Conduction: dQ/dt = kA(T₁ - T₂) / L
Stefan-Boltzmann Law: E = e σ T⁴
Wien's Displacement: λ_max · T = b ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K
First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW   (where ΔW = P ΔV)
Mayer's Relation: C_p - C_v = R
Adiabatic: PV^γ = Constant,   TV^(γ-1) = Constant   (γ = C_p/C_v)
Carnot Engine Efficiency: η = 1 - (T₂ / T₁) = W / Q₁
notes: Work done in isothermal expansion: W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁). Work done in adiabatic: W = (P₁V₁ - P₂V₂) / (γ - 1) = nR(T₁ - T₂) / (γ - 1).

subject: Physics
title: Simple Harmonic Motion & Pendulum
formula:
Displacement: x(t) = A sin(ωt + φ)
Velocity: v = dx/dt = ω√(A² - x²),   v_max = Aω (at mean position)
Acceleration: a = -ω²x,   a_max = Aω² (at extreme position)
Time Period of Simple Pendulum: T = 2π √(L / g)
Spring-Mass System: T = 2π √(m / k)
Total Energy in SHM: E = K + U = ½mω²(A² - x²) + ½mω²x² = ½mω²A² = Constant
notes: In SHM, acceleration is directly proportional to displacement and opposite in direction. Kinetic energy is maximum at mean position, potential energy is maximum at extremes.

subject: Physics
title: Wave Equation, Organ Pipes & Doppler
formula:
Wave Equation: y(x,t) = A sin(kx - ωt + φ),   k = 2π/λ,  ω = 2πν
Wave Speed: v = ν · λ = ω / k
Transverse wave on stretched string: v = √(T / μ)
Sound in gas (Newton-Laplace): v = √(γP / ρ) = √(γRT / M)
Organ Pipes:
Open Pipe: Fundamental f₁ = v / (2L),   Harmonics f_n = n · f₁ (1:2:3:4...)
Closed Pipe: Fundamental f₁ = v / (4L),   Harmonics f_n = (2n - 1)f₁ (1:3:5:7...)
Beat Frequency: f_beat = |f₁ - f₂|
Doppler Effect: f' = f · [ (v ± v_o) / (v ∓ v_s) ]
notes: Upper sign when observer/source moves towards each other (frequency increases); lower sign when moving away (frequency decreases).

subject: Chemistry
title: Concentration Terms & Limiting Reagent
formula:
Number of Moles: n = Mass / Molar Mass = N / N_A = Volume at STP(L) / 22.4
Molarity (M) = Moles of Solute / Volume of Solution (in L)
Molality (m) = Moles of Solute / Mass of Solvent (in kg)
Normality (N) = Molarity × n-factor (Gram equivalents / L)
Mole Fraction: x_A = n_A / (n_A + n_B),   x_A + x_B = 1
Dilution: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂,   Neutralization: N₁V₁ = N₂V₂
Mass % = (Mass of Solute / Total Mass of Solution) × 100
notes: N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. Limiting reagent is the reactant completely consumed first in a reaction and determines amount of product formed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bohr Model, de Broglie & Heisenberg
formula:
Bohr Energy: E_n = -13.6 · (Z² / n²) eV
Bohr Radius: r_n = 0.529 · (n² / Z) Å
Rydberg Formula: 1/λ = R_H · Z² · [ (1/n₁²) - (1/n₂²) ]   (R_H ≈ 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹)
de Broglie Wavelength: λ = h / p = h / (m v) = h / √(2m · K.E.)
Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle: Δx · Δp ≥ h / (4π)
Quantum Numbers: n (1,2,3..), l (0 to n-1), m_l (-l to +l), m_s (±½)
notes:
Spectral Series of Hydrogen:
Lyman (n₁=1, UV)
Balmer (n₁=2, Visible)
Paschen (n₁=3, IR)
Brackett (n₁=4, IR)
Pfund (n₁=5, IR). Hund's rule: pairing occurs only after each orbital has one electron.

subject: Chemistry
title: Periodic Trends & Anomalies
formula:
Atomic Radius: Decreases across period (effective nuclear charge Z_eff increases), Increases down group.
Ionization Enthalpy: Increases across period, Decreases down group.
Anomalies in IE:
IE₁(Be) > IE₁(B)  (Be has fully filled 2s² configuration)
IE₁(N) > IE₁(O)  (N has stable half-filled 2p³ configuration)
Electron Gain Enthalpy (Δ_egH): Cl has MORE negative Δ_egH than F (due to small size of F and interelectronic repulsions in 2p orbital).
Electronegativity: F (4.0) > O (3.5) > N (3.0) ≈ Cl (3.0) > Br (2.8) > C (2.5) ≈ I (2.5)
notes: Metallic character decreases across period and increases down group. Amphoteric oxides: Al₂O₃, ZnO, BeO, SnO, PbO.

subject: Chemistry
title: VSEPR, Hybridization & MOT
formula:
Formal Charge = V - N - ½B
Hybridization Steric Number: SN = ½[V + M - C + A]
VSEPR Geometry:
SN = 2: sp, Linear (180°)
SN = 3: sp², Trigonal Planar (120°)
SN = 4: sp³, Tetrahedral (109.5°)
SN = 5: sp³d, Trigonal Bipyramidal (90°, 120°)
SN = 6: sp³d², Octahedral (90°)
Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT):
Bond Order = ½(N_b - N_a)
Magnetic Nature: Unpaired electrons ⇒ Paramagnetic; All paired ⇒ Diamagnetic
notes: O₂ molecule has 16 electrons, Bond Order = 2, and is PARAMAGNETIC due to 2 unpaired electrons in π*2p_x and π*2p_y orbitals. Dipole moment μ = q × d (Debye).

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy, Hess's Law & Gibbs Energy
formula:
First Law: ΔU = q + w,   w = -P_ext ΔV (expansion)
Enthalpy: H = U + PV ⇒ ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT
Hess's Law: ΔH_reaction = Σ Δ_f H(Products) - Σ Δ_f H(Reactants)
Entropy: ΔS = q_rev / T
Gibbs Free Energy: ΔG = ΔH - T ΔS
Standard Gibbs Energy: ΔG° = -2.303 RT log₁₀ K_eq = -n F E°_cell
notes:
Spontaneity Criteria at constant T & P:
ΔG < 0: Spontaneous (exergonic)
ΔG = 0: System at equilibrium
ΔG > 0: Non-spontaneous (endergonic). For exothermic reactions (ΔH < 0), spontaneity favoured at low T.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chemical & Ionic Equilibrium, pH & Buffer
formula:
Equilibrium Relation: K_p = K_c (RT)^Δn_g
pH = -log₁₀[H⁺],   pOH = -log₁₀[OH⁻],   pH + pOH = 14 (at 298 K)
Ostwald's Dilution Law (weak electrolyte): K_a = Cα² / (1 - α) ≈ Cα² ⇒ α = √(K_a / C)
Buffer Solutions (Henderson-Hasselbalch):
Acidic Buffer: pH = pK_a + log([Salt] / [Acid])
Basic Buffer: pOH = pK_b + log([Salt] / [Base])
Solubility Product K_sp for A_x B_y ⇌ x A^(y+) + y B^(x-):
K_sp = [A^(y+)]ˣ [B^(x-)]ʸ = xˣ · yʸ · S^(x+y)
notes: Le Chatelier's Principle: If stress (P, T, concentration) is applied to equilibrium, system shifts in direction that counteracts the stress. Precipitation occurs when Ionic Product (Q_sp) > K_sp.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation Numbers & Balancing
formula:
Rules: Free elemental state = 0; Group 1 = +1; Group 2 = +2; Fluorine = -1; Oxygen = -2 (except peroxides = -1, OF₂ = +2); Hydrogen = +1 (except metal hydrides = -1).
Balancing by Ion-Electron Method (Half-Reaction Method):
1. Divide into Oxidation and Reduction halves.
2. Balance all atoms other than O and H.
3. Balance O by adding H₂O.
4. Balance H by adding H⁺ (in acidic medium).
5. Balance charges by adding electrons e⁻.
6. Equalize electrons in both halves and add together.
notes: Oxidizing agent undergoes reduction (oxidation number decreases). Reducing agent undergoes oxidation (oxidation number increases).

subject: Chemistry
title: IUPAC, Isomerism & Core Reactions
formula:
Stability of Intermediates:
Carbocations: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ (Stabilized by +I & Hyperconjugation)
Free Radicals: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃˙
Carbanions: CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3° (Stabilized by -I)
Core Named Reactions:
Wurtz Reaction: 2 R-X + 2 Na (dry ether) → R-R + 2 NaX
Kolbe Electrolysis: 2 RCOONa + 2 H₂O → R-R + 2 CO₂ + H₂ + 2 NaOH
Markownikoff's Rule: Negative part of addendum adds to carbon having fewer hydrogens.
Anti-Markownikoff (Peroxide/Kharasch): Applies ONLY to HBr with peroxides (free radical mechanism).
Ozonolysis of Alkenes: R-CH=CH-R + O₃/Zn-H₂O → 2 R-CHO (identifies double bond location)
Friedel-Crafts Alkylation: Benzene + R-Cl (anhydrous AlCl₃) → Alkylbenzene + HCl
notes: Huckel's Rule for Aromaticity: Cyclic, planar, completely conjugated ring with (4n + 2) π electrons (where n = 0, 1, 2...). Ortho/para directing groups: -OH, -NH₂, -CH₃, -OCH₃, -Cl. Meta directing: -NO₂, -CHO, -COOH, -CN.

subject: Biology
title: Five Kingdoms & Plant Groups
formula:
Whittaker's 5 Kingdoms (1969):
1. Monera: Prokaryotic, unicellular, peptidoglycan wall (Bacteria, Cyanobacteria, Archaebacteria)
2. Protista: Eukaryotic, unicellular (Amoeba, Euglena, Diatoms)
3. Fungi: Heterotrophic, chitinous cell wall (Yeast, Rhizopus, Agaricus)
4. Plantae: Autotrophic, cellulose wall (Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms)
5. Animalia: Heterotrophic, multicellular, lack cell wall
notes: Cyanobacteria have heterocysts for nitrogen fixation (e.g. Nostoc, Anabaena). Lichens are symbiotic associations of algae (phycobiont) and fungi (mycobiont).

subject: Biology
title: Organelles, Mitosis & Meiosis
formula:
Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic: 70S ribosomes (30S+50S) in prokaryotes; 80S (40S+60S) in eukaryotes.
Mitochondria: Double membrane, cristae, ATP synthesis by oxidative phosphorylation, circular DNA.
Chloroplast: Thylakoids in grana (light reaction), stroma (Calvin cycle).
Mitosis: Prophase, Metaphase (chromosomes align at equator), Anaphase (sister chromatids separate), Telophase.
Meiosis I Prophase I Stages:
1. Leptotene: Chromatin condenses
2. Zygotene: Synapsis of homologous chromosomes (synaptonemal complex)
3. Pachytene: Crossing over mediated by enzyme recombinase
4. Diplotene: Chiasmata visible
5. Diakinesis: Terminalisation of chiasmata
notes: S-phase of interphase is the DNA replication phase (amount of DNA doubles, chromosome number remains same). Meiosis results in 4 haploid genetically diverse daughter cells.

subject: Biology
title: Photosynthesis & Respiration
formula:
Photosynthesis Light Reactions: In thylakoid membranes; photolysis of water (2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂), non-cyclic photophosphorylation generates ATP and NADPH.
Dark Reaction (Calvin Cycle): In stroma; 3 steps: Carboxylation (catalyzed by RuBisCO, most abundant enzyme on Earth), Reduction, Regeneration. Fixes 1 CO₂ using 3 ATP + 2 NADPH.
C4 Pathway (Hatch-Slack): Kranz anatomy; avoids photorespiration; PEP carboxylase in mesophyll, RuBisCO in bundle sheath.
Respiration (Glycolysis): EMP pathway in cytoplasm; 1 Glucose → 2 Pyruvate, net gain 2 ATP + 2 NADH.
Krebs Cycle: In mitochondrial matrix; generates 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 GTP per acetyl-CoA.
Plant Hormones: Auxin (apical dominance), Gibberellin (bolting/internode elongation), Cytokinin (cell division), ABA (stress hormone/stomatal closure), Ethylene (gaseous/fruit ripening).
notes: Photorespiration is a wasteful process in C3 plants occurring in Chloroplast, Peroxisome and Mitochondria when RuBisCO binds O₂ instead of CO₂.

subject: Biology
title: Circulation, Excretion & Hormones
formula:
Circulation:
Heart Pacemaker: SA Node (generates 70-75 action potentials/min) → AV Node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibers.
ECG Waves: P wave (atrial depolarization), QRS complex (ventricular depolarization), T wave (ventricular repolarization).
Excretion (Nephron):
Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) ≈ 125 mL/min (180 L/day). 99% filtrate reabsorbed in PCT.
Counter-Current Mechanism: Between Loop of Henle and Vasa Recta, concentrates urine (up to 1200 mOsmol/L).
RAAS Mechanism: JGA cells release Renin when GFR falls → Angiotensinogen converted to Angiotensin II (vasoconstrictor) → Aldosterone released by adrenal cortex (reabsorbs Na⁺ and water).
Hormones:
Insulin (β-cells of islets): Lowers blood glucose (hypoglycemic).
Glucagon (α-cells): Raises blood glucose (hyperglycemic).
Adrenaline (Adrenal medulla): Emergency / Fight-or-Flight hormone.
notes: Normal blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg. Double circulation: Pulmonary (Heart → Lungs → Heart) and Systemic (Heart → Body → Heart).

subject: English
title: Notice Writing Format (CBSE Standard)
formula:
Box is MANDATORY. Max 50 Words.
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         NAME OF ISSUING AUTHORITY / SCHOOL    │
│                      NOTICE                   │
│ Date: DD Month YYYY                           │
│               CATCHY HEADING                  │
│ Body: State event details clearly:            │
│ - Date, Time, Venue                           │
│ - Purpose / Eligibility / Agenda             │
│ - Whom to contact for registration/details   │
│ Signature                                     │
│ NAME IN BLOCK LETTERS                         │
│ Designation                                   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
notes: Marking scheme: 1 Mark for Format (Box, Heading, Date, Signature), 2 Marks for Content, 1 Mark for Expression (Grammar & Spelling). Total = 4 Marks.

subject: English
title: Letter to the Editor Format
formula:
Sender's Address (2-3 lines)
Date: 19 November 2026

The Editor
Name of Newspaper (e.g. The Times of India)
City

Subject: [Concise, catchy and underlined]

Sir / Madam,

Para 1 (Introduction): Through the esteemed columns of your widely circulated daily, I wish to draw the attention of the concerned authorities and the public towards the pressing issue of [Problem]...

Para 2 (Content & Impact): Explain the problem in detail, causes, real-world consequences and hardships faced by the citizens...

Para 3 (Conclusion & Appeal): It is earnestly hoped that the relevant authorities will take swift and stringent measures to resolve this issue without delay.

Yours sincerely / Yours faithfully,
[Signature / Name]
notes: Word limit: 120-150 words. Total = 5 Marks (Format: 1, Content: 2, Expression: 2). Never write your real name if an assumed name is given in the question prompt.

subject: English
title: Speech & Debate Writing Framework
formula:
Speech Writing:
1. Catchy Title.
2. Formal Opening Salutation: 'Respected Principal, worthy teachers, and my dear friends, a very warm good morning to one and all present here. Today, I, [Name], stand before you to express my views on...'
3. Body: Define the issue, quote statistics, discuss pros and cons, suggest practical solutions.
4. Conclusion: Inspirational closing appeal / thought.
5. Closing: 'Thank you!'

Debate Writing:
1. Opening Salutation + Explicit Stand ('I firmly stand FOR / AGAINST the motion...').
2. Rebuttal to opposition arguments.
3. Logical arguments backed with facts.
4. Strong concluding punchline + 'Thank you.'
notes: Word limit: 120-150 words. Total = 5 Marks. Use rhetorical questions and persuasive connectors like 'Furthermore', 'On the contrary', 'Consequently'.

subject: English
title: Key Figures of Speech for Exams
formula:
1. Simile: Comparison using 'like' or 'as' (e.g. 'her face ashen like that of a corpse')
2. Metaphor: Direct implied comparison without like/as (e.g. 'the paper-seeming boy')
3. Personification: Giving human attributes to non-living objects (e.g. 'the tree stood mourning in silence')
4. Alliteration: Repetition of initial consonant sounds (e.g. 'clean clothes', 'stop and smile')
5. Oxymoron: Two contradictory terms juxtaposed together (e.g. 'laboured ease', 'sweet sorrow')
6. Onomatopoeia: Words that imitate natural sounds (e.g. 'buzz', 'rattle', 'clatter')
7. Hyperbole: Obvious intentional exaggeration for dramatic effect (e.g. 'rivers of blood flooded the field')
notes: Frequently asked in 1-Marker and 2-Marker poetry extract questions in Class 11 & 12 Board examinations.

subject: Maths
title: Types of Relations & Functions
formula:
Reflexive: (a, a) ∈ R ∀ a ∈ A
Symmetric: (a, b) ∈ R ⇒ (b, a) ∈ R
Transitive: (a, b) ∈ R and (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R
Equivalence: Reflexive + Symmetric + Transitive
One-One (Injective): f(x₁) = f(x₂) ⇒ x₁ = x₂
Onto (Surjective): Range = Codomain (∀ y ∈ Y ∃ x ∈ X such that f(x) = y)
Bijective: One-One + Onto (Invertible function)
notes: Essential for Class 12 Boards and JEE. A function f: X → Y has an inverse f⁻¹: Y → X if and only if f is bijective.

subject: Maths
title: Principal Value Branches & Properties
formula:
sin⁻¹x: [-1, 1] → [-π/2, π/2]
cos⁻¹x: [-1, 1] → [0, π]
tan⁻¹x: ℝ → (-π/2, π/2)
cot⁻¹x: ℝ → (0, π)
sec⁻¹x: ℝ - (-1, 1) → [0, π] - {π/2}
cosec⁻¹x: ℝ - (-1, 1) → [-π/2, π/2] - {0}
sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2   (x ∈ [-1, 1])
tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2   (x ∈ ℝ)
tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x + y)/(1 - xy))   (for xy < 1)
notes: Always check the principal branch range when evaluating inverse trig expressions to avoid negative sign traps.

subject: Maths
title: Matrix Operations, Inverse & Linear Systems
formula:
Matrix Multiplication: A_(m×n) · B_(n×p) = C_(m×p)
(A · B)ᵀ = Bᵀ · Aᵀ,   |A · B| = |A| · |B|
|k A| = kⁿ |A|  (for n×n matrix A)
Adjoint: A · adj(A) = adj(A) · A = |A| · Iₙ
|adj(A)| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹,   |adj(adj(A))| = |A|^( (n-1)² )
Inverse: A⁻¹ = (1 / |A|) · adj(A)   (|A| ≠ 0)
Matrix Method: A X = B  ⇒  X = A⁻¹ B
notes: If |A| = 0, matrix is singular (no unique inverse). For homogeneous AX = 0, non-trivial solution exists iff |A| = 0.

subject: Maths
title: Chain Rule, Logarithmic & Parametric
formula:
Continuity: lim_{x→c⁻} f(x) = lim_{x→c⁺} f(x) = f(c)
Chain Rule: (d/dx)[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) · g'(x)
Logarithmic: y = u(x)^v(x)  ⇒  dy/dx = y [v'(x) ln u(x) + (v(x)/u(x)) u'(x)]
Parametric: x = f(t), y = g(t)  ⇒  dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt)
d²y/dx² = [d/dt(dy/dx)] / (dx/dt)
notes: Take natural log on both sides when variable is in exponent or when dealing with long products/quotients.

subject: Maths
title: Monotonicity & Maxima-Minima
formula:
Strictly Increasing: f'(x) > 0 for all x ∈ (a, b)
Strictly Decreasing: f'(x) < 0 for all x ∈ (a, b)
Critical Point: x = c where f'(c) = 0 or f'(c) is undefined
Second Derivative Test:
- If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) < 0  ⇒  Local Maximum at x = c
- If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0  ⇒  Local Minimum at x = c
- If f''(c) = 0  ⇒  Use First Derivative Sign Change Test
notes: For absolute maxima/minima on closed interval [a, b], evaluate f(x) at critical points AND at boundary endpoints a and b.

subject: Maths
title: Standard Forms, Parts & King's Property
formula:
∫ (1 / (x² + a²)) dx = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) + C
∫ (1 / √(a² - x²)) dx = sin⁻¹(x/a) + C
∫ (1 / √(x² ± a²)) dx = ln|x + √(x² ± a²)| + C
Integration by Parts: ∫ u v dx = u ∫ v dx - ∫ [u' ∫ v dx] dx   (ILATE Order)
Definite King's Property: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b - x) dx
Symmetric Interval: ∫_{-a}^a f(x) dx = 0 (if f is odd), = 2 ∫_0^a f(x) dx (if f is even)
Periodicity: ∫_0^{nT} f(x) dx = n ∫_0^T f(x) dx  (if f(x+T) = f(x))
notes: King's property (x → a + b - x) solves 80% of board and JEE definite integrals by adding I + I.

subject: Maths
title: Variable Separable & Linear D.E.
formula:
Variable Separable: f(x) dx = g(y) dy  ⇒  integrate directly
Linear D.E. Form 1: dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x)
Integrating Factor (I.F.) = e^(∫ P(x) dx)
General Solution: y · (I.F.) = ∫ [Q(x) · (I.F.)] dx + C
Linear D.E. Form 2: dx/dy + P(y) x = Q(y)  ⇒  I.F. = e^(∫ P(y) dy)
Homogeneous: dy/dx = f(y/x)  ⇒  substitute y = v x, dy/dx = v + x (dv/dx)
notes: Always identify the independent variable first to choose whether Form 1 (dy/dx) or Form 2 (dx/dy) applies.

subject: Maths
title: Dot, Cross, Skew Lines & Plane
formula:
Dot Product: a · b = |a||b| cos θ = a_x b_x + a_y b_y + a_z b_z  (Perpendicular if a · b = 0)
Projection of a on b = (a · b) / |b|
Cross Product: a × b = |a||b| sin θ n̂  (Parallel if a × b = 0)
Direction Cosines: l² + m² + n² = 1
Equation of Line: (x - x₁)/a = (y - y₁)/b = (z - z₁)/c  (Vector: r = a + λ b)
Shortest Distance between Skew Lines (r = a₁ + λ b₁ and r = a₂ + μ b₂):
d = |(a₂ - a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|
notes: Lines intersect if shortest distance d = 0, meaning (a₂ - a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0 (coplanar).

subject: Maths
title: Conditional, Bayes' Theorem & Distributions
formula:
Conditional: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)   (P(B) > 0)
Independent Events: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B)
Total Probability: P(A) = Σ P(Eᵢ) · P(A | Eᵢ)
Bayes' Theorem: P(E_k | A) = [P(E_k) · P(A | E_k)] / [Σ P(Eᵢ) · P(A | Eᵢ)]
Random Variable Mean: μ = E(X) = Σ xᵢ pᵢ
Variance: σ² = Var(X) = E(X²) - [E(X)]² = Σ xᵢ² pᵢ - μ²
notes: Bayes' theorem is tested every year in 4-Marker/5-Marker questions. Clearly define partition events E₁, E₂, ... first.

subject: Physics
title: Coulomb's Law, Field & Gauss Flux
formula:
Coulomb's Law: F = (1 / 4πε₀) · (|q₁q₂| / r²)   (1/4πε₀ ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Electric Dipole: p = q · 2a
Torque on Dipole: τ = p × E = p E sin θ
Potential Energy: U = -p · E = -p E cos θ
Axial Field: E_axial = (2 k p) / r³   (r >> a)
Equatorial Field: E_equatorial = -(k p) / r³
Gauss's Law: Φ = ∮ E · dA = q_enclosed / ε₀
Infinite Line Charge: E = λ / (2πε₀ r)
Infinite Sheet: E = σ / (2ε₀)
notes: Field inside a charged spherical conductor is zero (E = 0); potential inside is uniform and equals surface potential.

subject: Physics
title: Potential, Energy & Capacitors
formula:
Potential: V = k q / r  (Relation: E = -dV/dr)
Capacitance: C = Q / V
Parallel Plate Capacitor: C₀ = ε₀ A / d   (With dielectric: C = K ε₀ A / d)
Energy Stored: U = ½ C V² = Q² / (2C) = ½ Q V
Energy Density: u = ½ ε₀ E²
Series Combination: 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ...
Parallel Combination: C_eq = C₁ + C₂ + ...
Common Potential after connection: V = (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂) / (C₁ + C₂)
Loss of Energy: ΔU = ½ · [C₁C₂ / (C₁ + C₂)] · (V₁ - V₂)²
notes: When battery remains connected, V is constant. When battery is disconnected, Q is constant.

subject: Physics
title: Drift, Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff & Cells
formula:
Drift Velocity: v_d = -(e E τ) / m
Current: I = n e A v_d
Current Density: j = I / A = σ E = E / ρ
Resistivity & Temp: R_T = R₀(1 + α ΔT)
Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): Σ I = 0   (Charge Conservation)
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): Σ ΔV = 0  (Energy Conservation)
Wheatstone Bridge: P / Q = R / S   (Null deflection in galvanometer)
Internal Resistance: r = R (E/V - 1)
Terminal Voltage: V = E - I r (discharging), V = E + I r (charging)
notes: Color code mnemonic: B B ROY of Great Britain had Very Good Wife (0 to 9).

subject: Physics
title: Biot-Savart, Ampere & Lorentz Force
formula:
Biot-Savart Law: dB = (μ₀ / 4π) · (I dl × r̂) / r²   (μ₀/4π = 10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
Center of Circular Loop: B = μ₀ I / (2R)
Axis of Circular Loop: B = (μ₀ I R²) / [2 (R² + x²)^(3/2)]
Ampere's Law: ∮ B · dl = μ₀ I_enclosed
Solenoid: B = μ₀ n I
Lorentz Force: F = q (E + v × B)
Magnetic Force on Wire: F = I (L × B)
Force between Parallel Wires: F / L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2π d)  (Attract if parallel, repel if antiparallel)
Torque on Loop: τ = M × B = N I A B sin θ
notes: Radius of helical path: r = m v_⊥ / (q B); Time period T = 2πm / (q B) (independent of speed).

subject: Physics
title: Faraday, Lenz, Reactance & Resonance
formula:
Magnetic Flux: Φ = B · A = B A cos θ
Faraday-Lenz Law: ε = -dΦ/dt
Motional EMF: ε = B v l
Self-Inductance: ε = -L (dI/dt),   U = ½ L I²
Mutual Inductance: ε₂ = -M (dI₁/dt)
RMS Values: I_rms = I₀ / √2 ≈ 0.707 I₀,   V_rms = V₀ / √2
Reactance: X_L = ω L,   X_C = 1 / (ω C)
Series LCR Impedance: Z = √[R² + (X_L - X_C)²]
Resonant Frequency: ω₀ = 1 / √(L C)  ⇒  f₀ = 1 / (2π√(LC))
Power Factor: cos φ = R / Z,   P_avg = V_rms I_rms cos φ
notes: At resonance, Z is minimum (Z = R), current is maximum, and circuit behaves as purely resistive.

subject: Physics
title: Lens Maker, Interference & Diffraction
formula:
Snell's Law: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r
Total Internal Reflection: sin θ_c = 1 / n
Refraction at Spherical Surface: (n₂ / v) - (n₁ / u) = (n₂ - n₁) / R
Lens Maker's Formula: 1/f = (n - 1) [1/R₁ - 1/R₂]
Thin Lens Formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u,   Magnification m = v / u
Young's Double Slit (YDSE):
- Fringe Width: β = λ D / d
- Bright Fringe: y_n = n λ D / d
- Dark Fringe: y_n = (2n - 1) λ D / (2d)
Single Slit Diffraction Minima: a sin θ = n λ
Central Maximum Angular Width = 2λ / a,   Linear Width = 2 λ D / a
notes: When light travels from rarer to denser medium, frequency remains constant, but wavelength and speed decrease.

subject: Physics
title: Photoelectric, Bohr, Nucleus & Diodes
formula:
Einstein's Photoelectric Eq: K_max = h ν - Φ₀ = e V₀
de Broglie Wavelength: λ = h / p = h / √(2mE) = 1.227 nm / √V  (for electron)
Bohr Model: m v r = n h / 2π
r_n = 0.529 (n² / Z) Å,   E_n = -13.6 (Z² / n²) eV
Rydberg Formula: 1/λ = R_H Z² [1/n₁² - 1/n₂²]
Mass Defect: Δm = [Z m_p + (A - Z) m_n] - M_nucleus
Binding Energy: BE = Δm × 931.5 MeV
p-n Junction: Forward bias (depletion layer narrows), Reverse bias (depletion layer widens)
Rectifier: Half-wave efficiency = 40.6%, Full-wave efficiency = 81.2%
notes: Work function Φ₀ depends only on metal surface material, not on intensity or frequency of incident light.

subject: Chemistry
title: Raoult's Law, Van 't Hoff & Osmosis
formula:
Raoult's Law: P_total = P°_A x_A + P°_B x_B
Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure: (P° - P) / P° = i · x_solute
Elevation in Boiling Point: ΔT_b = i · K_b · m
Depression in Freezing Point: ΔT_f = i · K_f · m
Osmotic Pressure: π = i · C R T
Van 't Hoff Factor (i):
- Dissociation: i = 1 + (n - 1) α
- Association: i = 1 + (1/n - 1) α
Henry's Law: P = K_H · x
notes: Ideal solutions follow Raoult's law over entire range (ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0, e.g. Benzene + Toluene).

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst Equation, Kohlrausch & Faraday
formula:
Nernst Equation (at 298 K): E_cell = E°_cell - (0.0591 / n) log₁₀ Q
Equilibrium Constant: log₁₀ K_c = (n E°_cell) / 0.0591
Gibbs Free Energy: ΔG° = -n F E°_cell
Kohlrausch's Law: Λ°_m = ν₊ λ°₊ + ν₋ λ°₋
Degree of Dissociation: α = Λ_m / Λ°_m
Dissociation Constant: K_a = (c α²) / (1 - α)
Faraday's 1st Law: m = Z · I · t = (M / (n F)) · Q
notes: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) has E° = 0.00 V. Positive E°_cell means cell reaction is spontaneous.

subject: Chemistry
title: Rate Law, Integrated Equations & Arrhenius
formula:
Zero Order: [A] = [A]₀ - k t,   t_½ = [A]₀ / (2k)   (k unit: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹)
First Order: k = (2.303 / t) log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]),   t_½ = 0.693 / k   (k unit: s⁻¹)
Arrhenius Equation: k = A e^(-Ea / RT)
log₁₀(k₂ / k₁) = (Ea / 2.303 R) [ (T₂ - T₁) / (T₁ T₂) ]
Pseudo First Order: Reaction where one reactant is in large excess (e.g. ester hydrolysis in water)
notes: For a 1st order reaction, half-life t_½ is independent of initial concentration [A]₀.

subject: Chemistry
title: Werner, Crystal Field & Nomenclature
formula:
Werner's Theory: Primary Valency = Oxidation State (ionizable); Secondary Valency = Coordination Number (non-ionizable)
Crystal Field Splitting: Octahedral Δ₀ (t_2g lower by 0.4Δ₀, e_g higher by 0.6Δ₀)
Tetrahedral Splitting: Δ_t = (4/9) Δ₀
Spectrochemical Series: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO
Strong Field Ligands: Pairing occurs (Low Spin, Inner Orbital d²sp³)
Weak Field Ligands: Pairing does NOT occur (High Spin, Outer Orbital sp³d²)
Magnetic Moment: μ = √(n(n + 2)) BM  (n = number of unpaired electrons)
notes: Colour in coordination complexes arises from d-d transitions when d-orbitals are partially filled (d¹ to d⁹).

subject: Chemistry
title: S_N1/S_N2, Aldol, Cannizzaro & Amines
formula:
S_N1 Mechanism: 2-step, carbocation intermediate, 3° > 2° > 1°, racemization
S_N2 Mechanism: 1-step concerted, backside attack, 1° > 2° > 3°, Walden inversion
Aldol Condensation: Carbonyl with α-H + dil. NaOH  ⇒  β-hydroxy aldehyde/ketone  ⇒  α,β-unsaturated
Cannizzaro Reaction: Carbonyl without α-H (HCHO, C₆H₅CHO) + conc. NaOH  ⇒  Alcohol + Salt of acid
Clemmensen Reduction: C=O + Zn-Hg / conc. HCl  ⇒  CH₂
Wolff-Kishner: C=O + NH₂NH₂ / KOH  ⇒  CH₂
Carbylamine Test: 1° Amine + CHCl₃ + 3KOH  ⇒  foul smelling isocyanide (R-NC)
Hinsberg Test: Benzenesulfonyl chloride (1° amine product dissolves in alkali, 2° does not)
notes: Lucas Test: 3° alcohol turns cloudy immediately, 2° in 5 minutes, 1° only on heating.

subject: Biology
title: Flowering Plants & Human Reproduction
formula:
Double Fertilization in Angiosperms: Syngamy (Egg + Sperm → 2n Zygote) + Triple Fusion (Central Cell + Sperm → 3n Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN)
Male Reproductive: Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens
Spermatogenesis: Spermatogonia (2n) → 1° Spermatocyte (2n) → 2° Spermatocyte (n) → Spermatids (n) → Sperm (n)
Oogenesis: Primary oocyte arrested at Prophase-I until puberty. Ovulation triggered by LH surge (releases 2° oocyte arrested at Metaphase-II)
Menstrual Cycle: Menstrual (1-5 d) → Follicular/Proliferative (6-13 d) → Ovulatory (14th d, LH surge) → Luteal/Secretory (15-28 d, Progesterone by Corpus luteum)
notes: Oxytocin from posterior pituitary stimulates uterine contractions during parturition (positive feedback reflex).

subject: Biology
title: Mendelism, DNA Replication & Lac Operon
formula:
Mendel's Ratios: Monohybrid F₂ phenotypic 3:1, genotypic 1:2:1. Dihybrid F₂ phenotypic 9:3:3:1
Incomplete Dominance: 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White (Snapdragon / Mirabilis jalapa)
Co-dominance: ABO Blood Group (Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i)
Sickle Cell Anemia: Point mutation in β-globin gene (GAG → GUG: Glutamic acid replaced by Valine at 6th position)
DNA Structure: Watson-Crick double helix, 10 bp/turn, 3.4 nm pitch, A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)
Meselson & Stahl: Demonstrated semi-conservative replication using ¹⁵N and ¹⁴N isotopes
Lac Operon: Repressor protein (i gene) binds Operator (o). Inducer (Lactose/Allolactose) binds repressor, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe z (β-galactosidase), y (permease), a (transacetylase)
notes: AUG has dual functions: codes for Methionine AND acts as the universal initiator codon.

subject: English
title: Invitations, Job Application & Articles
formula:
Formal Invitation (Card Format):
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Mrs. and Mr. Sharma request the pleasure of   │
│ your benign company on the auspicious occasion│
│ of the WEDDING of their son ROHIT with PRIYA  │
│ Date: 25 December 2026, Time: 7:00 PM         │
│ Venue: Grand Palace, MG Road, New Delhi       │
│ RSVP: Sharma Family, Contact: 98765xxxxx      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Job Application (Letter + Bio-Data):
1. Covering Letter (3 paragraphs: source of ad, suitability, enclosed resume).
2. Bio-Data / Resume: Personal Details, Educational Qualifications (tabular), Work Experience, References (2 persons).
notes: Job application with Bio-Data is worth 5 marks in Class 12 Boards. The tabular educational qualification carries method marks.
